display_title: [consts] Update migration docs for when we flip use_simplified_jaxpr_…

head_commit.message:
[consts] Update migration docs for when we flip use_simplified_jaxpr_constants

Also, bump the max size for constants that are allowed to be inlined.
Experiments show that up to 1024 bytes there are still constants for
which the compiler can profitably do constant-folding. This flag has no
effect until we turn on use_simplified_jaxpr_constants.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Treat negative indices as out of bounds in the TPU interpreter

head_commit.message:
Treat negative indices as out of bounds in the TPU interpreter

On TPU, Pallas does not wrap negative indices: Mosaic computes the
address as base + i * stride, so for x_ref[-1] the address lies before
the buffer. With --xla_mosaic_on_device_checks=bounds, the TPU reports
this as an out-of-bounds access.

The interpreter instead passed integer indices in [-n, -1] to NumPy,
which wraps them, so a read of x_ref[-1] returned the last row. A DMA
write to a negative index failed the bare `assert 0 <= r` in
is_range_out_of_bounds_for_shape.

Make clip_range_to_shape and is_range_out_of_bounds_for_shape treat a
negative integer index as out of bounds, so these accesses take the
existing out-of-bounds read and write paths. The Mosaic GPU interpreter
shares both functions.

Related to #27490.
